dial.summary: Democrats swept both Congressional chambers in US midterm elections (Nov 3), pushing DXY to ~101.32 and Treasury yields lower (10Y ~4.90%), though risk assets sold off on fiscal uncertainty; macro backdrop remains constructive with 5/8 indicators supportive — Global M2 rising, ISM Manufacturing at 55.5 (10th expansion month), real yields falling, Fed balance sheet flat, and BTC funding rates near zero post-Oct 30 liquidation reset — while BTC.D holds firm at ~60% with TOTAL at $2.60T and no alt-rotation catalyst in sight; BTC Accumulation posture intact.

indicators.name: Global Liquidity (Global M2)
indicators.note: MacroMicro G4 aggregate (US/Euro Zone/China/Japan) remains at ~$104.3T as of September 2026 (104,317B vs 103,624B in August); October 2026 data not yet available — MacroMicro typically updates mid-month following the reference month; next G4 update expected mid-November 2026; US M2 at $23.41T in Sep 2026 (+5.7% YoY) confirms no YoY contraction; GoldSilverHQ cited +12.05% YoY as of Feb 2026, trending higher into mid-year; 4-week Aug→Sep change +$0.64T (+0.6%) exceeds 0.5% flat threshold — trend remains UP; Bitrue estimates global M2 at $103.66T on a broader global basis; status supportive (4-week trend up); value and trend held unchanged from Nov 3 run — October G4 data publication pending.

indicators.name: ISM Manufacturing PMI
indicators.note: October 2026 ISM Manufacturing PMI printed 55.5% (released November 2, 2026 at 10:00 AM ET), beating consensus of 54.6% and up 1.0pp from September's 54.5%; 10th consecutive month of expansion; Production sub-index surged to 59.0 (highest since November 2021), New Orders at 55.5; Prices remained elevated at 75.2 (9th straight reading above 70); 4-week trend UP (Sep 54.5 → Oct 55.5, +1.0pp); status supportive (above 50 and rising); next ISM Manufacturing release December 1, 2026 (November data); value unchanged from Nov 3 run — monthly series, October reading already captured.

indicators.name: DXY (US Dollar Index)
indicators.note: ICE DXY spot ~101.32 intraday November 4, 2026 (FXStreet midterm election coverage: 'DXY is down 0.52% on the day at 101.32', intraday low 101.25, brief bounce to 101.48); Nov 3 close ~101.54 (Trading Economics); DXY under pressure as Democrats sweep both Congressional chambers — EUR/USD and GBP/USD strengthening on fiscal restraint expectations; 4-week trend FLAT — from ~101.5-102.0 range (Oct 5-7) to 101.32 (Nov 4), net change approximately within 0.5% flat threshold despite intraday pressure; 52-week high remains 102.95 on October 14, 2026; status headwind (above 100 threshold — DXY must fall below 97.5 for supportive).

indicators.name: Real Yields (US10Y - CPI)
indicators.note: 10-year TIPS real yield (DFII10) confirmed at 2.63% on October 29, 2026 (Macrotrends/ALFRED); prior run captured 2.60% on October 30, consistent with continued decline; FRED API not accessible in this session for Nov 3-4 update — holding at 2.60% (Oct 30) as the confirmed last observation; Nov 3 nominal 10Y fell further to ~4.902% (CNBC) on Democrat midterm wins, suggesting real yields may have declined slightly to ~2.57-2.60%; 4-week trend DOWN — from ~2.93% on September 29 to 2.60% on October 30, -33bps; 52-week range 1.72% (Feb 27, 2026) to 2.95% (Oct 5, 2026); status supportive (falling trend); absolute level 2.60% remains restrictive but directional improvement clear heading into December 8-9 FOMC.

indicators.name: 2s10s Yield Curve
indicators.note: November 4, 2026: 10Y ~4.90%, 2Y ~4.566% (FXStreet early Nov 4 midterm coverage), spread ~+33bps; Nov 3 CNBC close: 10Y down 5bps to 4.902%, 2Y down 6bps to 4.55%, spread ~35bps; using +34bps as midpoint of Nov 3-4 observations (up slightly from prior run's +32bps as 10Y declined more than 2Y on Democrat sweep and bond safe-haven bid); 4-week trend DOWN — from ~+42bps on October 1 to ~+34bps on November 4, -8bps flattening over the period; Democrats winning both chambers pushes 10Y lower on fiscal restraint expectations (smaller deficits) while 2Y remains sticky on Dec 8-9 FOMC odds; curve positive (well above -50bps headwind threshold); status neutral (positive but flattening, not steepening).

indicators.name: Fed Balance Sheet
indicators.note: WALCL latest confirmed reading: October 28, 2026 at $6,745,635M ($6.75T) per prior H.4.1 data; American Action Forum reports $6.7T, down $8B from prior week as of Oct 28, consistent with the Oct 21→Oct 28 decline from $6,753,604M to $6,745,635M; 4-week change Sep 30 to Oct 28 ≈ +$2.6B, essentially flat; next H.4.1 release November 5, 2026 (covering week ending Nov 5) — balance sheet value will be updated in tomorrow's run; oscillating in a narrow ~$12B band around $6.75T; status supportive (flat post-QT-pause stabilization, no aggressive QT, overnight rates stable).

indicators.name: BTC Funding Rates (perps avg)
indicators.note: CoinGlass not accessible in this session (domain not reachable from cloud environment); holding last reliable snapshot of ~0.0087% per 8h OI-weighted (from ~Oct 23); post-October 30 crash ($1.49B liquidations, 86.8% longs flushed) compressed funding toward near-zero — Glassnode snippet showed 0.002% (undated), CMC Academy reported 'Bitcoin Funding Rates Hit 3-Year Lows After Historic Liquidation'; Convex showed 0.00% rate alongside ~$74K BTC; FXStreet Nov 4 notes 'Bitcoin struggles to capitalize on US Dollar weakness as Democrats advance in midterms', suggesting no aggressive long positioning; 30-day trend DOWN (declining from pre-crash elevated levels through post-crash reset); status supportive (near zero, well below 0.04% headwind threshold); skipped — value held at last confirmed snapshot.

indicators.name: Stablecoin Dominance
indicators.note: DefiLlama stablecoin market cap $293.787B (November 3, 2026); CoinGecko snapshot ~$298B (marked potentially stale), reporting 11.23% share of total; total crypto market cap ~$2.60-2.61T (cryptoticker October 2026 recap: fell from $2.86T on Oct 1 to $2.60T on Nov 1; Au79 Macro Research Nov 3 commentary: $2.61T, -3.6% on the day); implied dominance $293.787B/$2.61T ≈ 11.26% → 11.3%; 30-day trend UP — Oct 5 stablecoin dom ~10.7% (est. $305B/$2.86T) → Nov 4 ~11.3%; rising dominance driven by crypto market cap compression (Oct 30 crash) with stablecoins only slightly down from their highs; BTC.D ~59.3-60.0% (Nov 2026, tv-hub.org); status neutral — headwind requires rising dom AND rising TOTAL simultaneously; TOTAL declining from Oct crash, so headwind condition not met; CoinGecko direct fetch unavailable this session.

upcoming.title: US Employment Situation — NFP (October 2026)
upcoming.note: BLS releases October 2026 nonfarm payrolls at 8:30 AM ET — the critical December 8-9 FOMC input; September NFP was +29K (weakest of the cycle); a rebound toward 100K+ would stabilize the labor narrative and support December hiking expectations, sustaining DXY headwind; a second consecutive sub-50K print would shift FOMC pricing toward a hold and could provide macro relief for risk assets recovering from the October 30 crash; Democrats' midterm sweep (Nov 3) adds political dimension — a weak print would validate dovish fiscal concerns.

upcoming.title: CPI (October 2026)
upcoming.note: BLS releases October 2026 Consumer Price Index at 8:30 AM ET — key inflation input for December 8-9 FOMC; September CPI was 3.7% YoY; October ISM Manufacturing Prices Index at 75.2 (9th consecutive reading above 70) signals ongoing cost pressure; a deceleration toward 3.0% could accelerate the real yield decline and ease headwinds on risk assets; a sustained print above 3.5% reinforces the case for a December 25bp hike and keeps DXY above 100; this is the dominant data print of the week.

upcoming.title: Initial Jobless Claims (week ended November 8, 2026)
upcoming.note: DOL weekly initial jobless claims at 8:30 AM ET for the week ended November 8 — released Thursday November 12 (Veterans Day November 11 is a federal holiday; bond markets close, equity and crypto remain open); the final weekly labor read before the December FOMC blackout period (Nov 28–Dec 10); context shaped by October NFP (Nov 6) and CPI (Nov 10) results; will be parsed closely as the last read before the Fed enters radio silence.
